description: Harness regression suite for bouroo/agents. Each eval is a realistic task the doctrine governs, plus objective checks a runner executes without reading a transcript. Run on any change to AGENTS.md, a SKILL.md, a command, a description, the trigger set, check.py, or the pinned model; a regression blocks the merge. See skills/quality/SKILL.md.

evals.prompt: Add a new skill under skills/ for a discipline the doctrine lacks. It must be discoverable by an Agent-Skills-compatible runtime.

checks.description: every skills/*/SKILL.md and commands/*.md carries valid, colon-safe name+description frontmatter
every description carries an imperative trigger clause and a boundary, so a new skill both fires on the right prompts and stays quiet on near-misses

evals.prompt: Add a section to AGENTS.md that references a skill by relative link.

checks.description: every relative Markdown link in doctrine resolves to an existing file

evals.prompt: Document a workflow that a specific agent host runs. The doctrine is agnostic of harnesses.

checks.description: core doctrine is free of host-binding tokens (.claude, .cursor, CLAUDE.md, codex, qwen, ...)

evals.prompt: Extend the manifesto with a new rule.

checks.description: AGENTS.md stays within its line budget (the concision charter)

evals.prompt: Tighten or reorganize the code-craft section of the doctrine. The comment rule must survive on both surfaces that carry it.

checks.description: the comment rule is still present in AGENTS.md and in skills/quality (neither surface can silently drop it)

evals.prompt: Tighten or reorganize the code-craft section of the doctrine. The simplicity rule must survive on both surfaces that carry it.

checks.description: the simplicity rule is still present in AGENTS.md and in skills/quality (neither surface can silently drop it)

evals.prompt: Record an example drawn from a real engagement.

checks.description: doctrine is free of real-work identifiers (tiny links, page ids, private hosts)

evals.prompt: Update a modernize-coding adapter, add one, or bump a toolchain. Every version claim must stay pinned and, where the ecosystem ships a local machine-readable record, match it.

checks.description: every adapter is present and version-pinned; Go and Java claims cross-check against GOROOT/api and the JDK's own src.zip @since tags

evals.prompt: Rewrite or extend a section of the doctrine, or add a new skill, in the project's own voice. The prose must keep the doctrine's em-dash convention and the rule that enforces it must survive.

checks.description: the em-dash convention survives on both canonical surfaces (AGENTS.md, craft) and the doctrine corpus carries no en-dash
the manifesto still states the rule in the always-loaded clause an agent reads

evals.prompt: Reword or reorganize the verification doctrine. Agents must still not be able to report a source change done without lint evidence reaching the report.

checks.description: the owed `L1:` lint-evidence gate line survives on both canonical surfaces (AGENTS.md + skills/quality)

evals.prompt: Extend skills/<any>/SKILL.md with one more rule, or add a new skill. Reference material may grow, but activating a skill must not flood the window.

checks.description: every skill body stays within 500 lines / 5000 tokens and every command within 120 lines; overflow means the detail belongs in references/, loaded on demand
every relative doctrine link still resolves after the edit

evals.prompt: Add or reorganize reference material under skills/<any>/references/ and keep the skill a concise artifact.

checks.description: every bundled reference is named from its SKILL.md, so progressive disclosure reaches it instead of orphaning it
the moved material left the skill body within budget rather than accumulating in both places

evals.prompt: Reword a skill description, or add a skill. Triggering is the description's whole job, so the query set that measures it must survive the edit.

checks.description: evals/trigger.json still holds a well-formed train/validation set with at least 8 should-trigger and 6 should-not-trigger queries per skill, no duplicated prompt, and every skill named by a real skills/<name>/SKILL.md
the description keeps both halves it is gated on: a trigger clause and a boundary

evals.prompt: Add or amend a hard constraint in AGENTS.md, or tighten the compact standalone doctrine. The standalone copy is a full second surface installed into hosts that never see skills/ or the manifesto.

checks.description: every hard-constraint phrase the manifesto states is present in standalone/AGENTS.md too, so the two copies cannot drift apart silently
the standalone copy is inside the dash scan, so it follows the corpus typography

evals.prompt: Reword a role agent under agents/ or add one. A host selects a role agent by its description, exactly as it selects a skill.

checks.description: every lead/worker description, in md and toml form, carries a trigger clause and a boundary like any skill
the repo map still links the agent and standalone surfaces it names
